title: Aream & Co：Q3 游戏行业并购总额达 578 亿美元，含 EA 550 亿美元杠杆收购
content:
Aream & Co: Games industry M&A generates $57.8 bn in Q3, including EA's $55bn leveraged buyout | GamesIndustry.biz

The number of games industry mergers and acquisitions stayed steady in the third quarter with 54 transactions totalling $57.8 billion, according to investment bank Aream & Co.
This included the completion of the
$55 billion leveraged buyout of Electronic Arts
, which took place on August 5.
Aream & Co.'s Video Game Market Update saw content-focused M&A accelerate, with 18 control deals for developers and publishers valued at more than $100 million year-to-date.
Deal activity was concentrated in Asia, which included Alibaba's sale of Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital for more than $1.5 billion, Netmarble founder Bang Jun-hyuk's acquisition of Tencent's stake in the company for $270 million, and Sony Music Entertainment's $180 million minority stake in GungHo.
Public market revenue leapt 122% year-on-year to $1.3 billion across 13 deals in Q3 2026. Aream & Co noted more listings in the pipeline, including Catalyst announcing the pricing of its $200 million IPO alongside PlaySimple and
Fellowship preparing to go public
.
Private investment revenue more than tripled year-on-year to $2.8 billion across 137 deals. Late-stage rounds reached $2.0 billion, the highest since Q4 2021. Seed funding fell to a five-year low as capital shifted to Series A funding.
Looking at consumer spending, PC sustained double-digit growth led by co-op and indie titles, including new IP Wardogs,
which generated $103 million in Q3,
according to data from Alinea Analytics.
Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynched came in second at $55 million, followed by Dazed Games' How to Fish at $11 million.
Mobile in-app purchases declined 7% YoY to $19.6 billion due to a smaller install base, though Turkish and Asian publishers continued to gain shares.
Console segment revenue dropped 12% YoY to $14.1 billion, which Aream & Co described as "the steepest drop in two years", marked by declines across all three platforms. Nintendo was down 18%, followed by Xbox at 10% and PlayStation at 9%.
Recent data from Circana found that in the US specifically,
hardware unit sales fell 15% year-on-year
to 559,000 in August, the lowest August total since 2013.
FC27 was the top-grossing release on console, having moved 4.9 million units during the quarter, followed by NBA 2K27 at 2.4 million and Wolverine at 2.1 million.
